description: Course capstone synthesizing Lozano–Valiente 2004, Droschinsky 2016 and 2018, independently specified witnesses, recurrences, matching-family speedups, existing Lean correctness, exact/source/numeric boundaries, and three worked proof-completion targets: fixed-root 2018 M1/M2, optimized matching deletion-family source refinement, and original-node/path decoding for NetworkX.

related_resources.reason: Ordered-tree contractions, balanced-word decomposition and the source-definition discrepancy.
Strict weighted subtree isomorphism, child matching, fixed-root reduction and deletion-family optimization.
Topological embedding score, mapped/skipped states, M1/M2 split and the optimized runtime argument.
Independent specifications, proof statements, induction, refinement and executable theorem reading.
Pinned Rust-to-Lean translation approach for the exact-integer source-level matching boundary.

learning_objectives: Contrast the three independent admissibility relations using a small path example, including 2018 penalty-dependent optimum changes.
Derive the shared witness-decomposition/assembly strategy without conflating ordered contraction, induced isomorphism or path embedding.
Explain how recurrence, executable table, witness reconstruction, source refinement and resource proofs compose.
State the 2018 fixed-first-root M1/M2 completeness and soundness targets and the needed highest-vertex and path-separation lemmas.
Formulate direct and transposed rectangular matching-deletion refinement and the separate amortized source-work obligation.
Formulate a conditional Python/NetworkX indexed-witness decoding theorem with original identities, paths, score and empty-policy correspondence.
Identify which proofs are checked in the November 2026 snapshot and which proposed theorem interfaces are open.
